title: Bogoliubov self-consistent $GW$ and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
authors: Mauricio Rodr{í}guez-Mayorga, Johannes Tölle, Pierre-François Loos
abstract: Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov fully self-consistent $GW$ (Bog.~sc$GW$) and second-order Green's function (Bog.~scGF2) methods, implemented within a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework. Using the attractive Hubbard model as a benchmark against full configuration interaction (FCI), we find that Bog. scGF2 provides a more accurate description than Bog.~sc$GW$. In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. These results highlight the importance of exchange contributions in strongly correlated fermionic systems, even when exchange effects are included only at low order in perturbation theory.
summary: This work investigates advanced many-body techniques, specifically Bogoliubov self-consistent GW and second-order Green's function methods, to treat attractive fermionic interactions. By benchmarking these methods against the exact Full Configuration Interaction result using the attractive Hubbard model, the authors demonstrate that the GF2 approach is superior to GW, particularly as the attractive interaction strength increases.
main_problem: The central challenge is accurately describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level.
main_result: The second-order Green's function method (Bog. scGF2) was found to provide a more accurate description of correlation energy than the fully self-consistent GW approach (Bog. scGW).
method: The authors compare Bogoliubov fully self-consistent GW (Bog. scGW) and second-order Green's function (Bog. scGF2) methods, implemented in a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework.
model_or_system: The study uses the attractive Hubbard model as a benchmark system to test the theoretical methods. The formalism builds upon the Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (HFB) approach, which is extended to include dynamical correlation effects.
key_observables: Total energies, anomalous density ($\kappa$), and the generalized (Gorkov) density matrix ($\mathbf{R}$).
important_parameters: The strength of the attractive interaction, which is varied to test the stability and accuracy of the methods.
main_assumptions: The HFB formalism is used as the starting point, which neglects dynamical correlation effects. The GW and GF2 methods are approximations used to recover these missing correlation terms.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by first establishing the HFB ground state, then introducing the GW and GF2 corrections, and finally comparing their quantitative results against the benchmark FCI calculation.
why_interesting: The comparison between GW and GF2 methods for strongly correlated systems provides valuable insight into the relative accuracy of different many-body perturbation theories when dealing with pairing mechanisms relevant to superconductivity.

The parameter t denotes the nearest-neighbor hopping amplitude between lattice sites, while U represents the on-site interaction between fermions of opposite spin (attractive in the present work). Blue and red arrows depict spin-up and spin-down fermions, respectively.

FIG. 2: Error in the total energy per electron with respect to FCI, ∆E/N = (E −EFCI)/N [(a) and (b)], and magnitude of the anomalous density, ∥κ∥2 [(c) and (d)], versus U/t for the 2 × 8 lattice with N = 6 [(a) and (c)] and the 4 × 4 lattice with N = 10 [(b) and (d)]. The horizontal line in (a) and (b) marks the FCI reference (∆E/N = 0).
